issues.t: Supercharger oil seal leak and blue smoke
issues.sym: Puffs of blue-gray smoke from the tailpipe, especially right after a cold start, and the oil level dropping quickly between changes. Oil may be visible in the intake ducts or around the supercharger pulley.
issues.why: The Millenia S uses a Lysholm screw-type supercharger whose internal oil seals are fragile. When they wear out, engine oil gets pulled into the intake and burned. Owners note the blower can still sound normal and make full boost while it is leaking.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and top it up so the engine is never run low. Have a shop look inside the intake for oil. A rebuilt supercharger is the usual fix; when it is replaced, the intercooler and pipes should be flushed and the PCV system checked.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping, stuck in gear or HOLD light flashing
issues.sym: The transmission stays in one gear (often first), shifts harshly or slips, and the HOLD or TCS lights may flash. Some owners hear a bang on shifts. Turning the car off and back on can clear it temporarily.
issues.why: The Millenia's 4-speed automatic can develop internal wear or electronic control faults. When the computer sees a problem it puts the transmission in a limp mode, which is what the flashing HOLD light signals.
issues.next: Have the transmission computer codes read and check the fluid level and condition. Avoid hard driving until it is diagnosed. A sensor, solenoid or wiring fault is cheaper to fix than a worn-out transmission, which may need a rebuild or a used replacement.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket leak causing misfires
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the top of the engine, a burning-oil smell, and a rough or stumbling engine when you accelerate. The check engine light may flash.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets harden with age. Oil then runs into the spark plug wells and soaks the plugs and boots, which causes misfires under load. Mazda issued a bulletin on valve cover oil leaks for these cars.
issues.next: Have the valve cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals replaced, and clean or replace any oil-soaked plugs and boots at the same time.

issues.t: EGR valve failure with shaking and check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often with an EGR code such as P0400, and the car may shake or run rough, getting worse at highway speeds.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve sticks or fails. It sits at the back of the V6, which makes it hard to reach and raises the labor cost.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the EGR valve and its vacuum lines tested before replacing parts. Cracked vacuum lines can cause the same code and are much cheaper to fix.

issues.t: Oxygen sensor failure and check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light stays on, sometimes with a code for an oxygen sensor (such as P0154), and fuel economy may drop. The car can fail a state emissions inspection.
issues.why: The upstream oxygen sensors on this V6 wear out and their built-in heaters fail. Some owners have had to replace the same sensor more than once.
issues.next: Have the codes read to confirm which sensor is at fault, and check its wiring. Replace failed sensors with good-quality parts so the light does not come back.

issues.t: Knock sensor code P0325 turns on check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0325. The car usually drives normally, though power can feel slightly down.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for check engine lights caused by knock sensor code P0325 on these cars. The knock sensor sits in the valley of the V6 under the intake, so a fault in the sensor or its wiring takes a lot of labor to reach.
issues.next: Have a Mazda-savvy shop check the bulletin fix and test the sensor wiring first. If the sensor itself must be replaced, plan for several hours of labor.

issues.t: Misfire codes P0300-P0306 and rough running
issues.sym: A rough idle or stumbling, a flashing or steady check engine light, and misfire codes from P0300 to P0306.
issues.why: Mazda put out a service bulletin for misfire codes on the Millenia. Fouled spark plugs, oil in the plug wells and tired ignition parts are common causes on these aging V6 engines.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the plugs, wires and plug wells inspected. Don't drive hard with a flashing check engine light, as raw fuel can overheat the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Water pump coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips or dried coolant crust at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, and the coolant level dropping. The temperature gauge may climb if it gets low.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears and starts weeping. Mazda issued an inspection procedure for water pump leaks on these cars. The pump is driven by the timing belt, so getting to it is a big job.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and have the leak confirmed. Replace the water pump together with the timing belt and tensioner to save on labor.

issues.t: Clunking or knocking from the front suspension
issues.sym: A knock, thump or clunk from the front end when going over bumps, or squeaks and scraping when turning the wheel.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for knocking or clunking noises from the front suspension. Worn bushings, links and strut parts are common on cars this age.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected for worn links, bushings and strut mounts. Replace worn parts in pairs so the car handles evenly.

issues.t: Creak or squeak from the rear suspension
issues.sym: A creaking or squeaking sound from the rear of the car over bumps or when the car rocks.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for creaks and squeaks from the rear suspension. Dry or worn rubber bushings are the usual source.
issues.next: Have a shop locate the noise. Bushing service or replacement usually quiets it; it is not usually a safety issue.

issues.t: TCS and TCS OFF lights on with ABS codes 83/84
issues.sym: The TCS and TCS OFF warning lights come on and stay on. Traction control and sometimes ABS may stop working.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for these lights coming on with trouble codes 83 and 84 stored in the ABS/traction control module.
issues.next: Have the ABS/TCS codes read by a shop with Mazda-capable equipment. Brakes still work normally, but drive carefully in rain and snow until it is fixed.

issues.t: Tapping noise from the engine when cold
issues.sym: A tapping or metallic ticking from the top of the engine, mostly right after a cold start, often from the right rear cylinder head.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins on cold tapping noises and a metallic tapping from the exhaust camshaft area of the rear cylinder head. Valve train wear and oil condition play a part.
issues.next: Make sure the oil is the right grade and is changed on time. If the tapping is loud or continues once warm, have the valve train checked.

issues.t: Whining or ringing noise inside the car
issues.sym: A whine or ringing sound heard inside the cabin while driving.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for a whine or ringing noise that was traced to the transmission and a related cable.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer or specialist about the bulletin fix. It is usually a nuisance rather than a sign of transmission failure.

issues.t: Tilt steering wheel stuck or not working
issues.sym: The power tilt steering wheel will not move, or it gets stuck in the up position.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for an inoperative tilt steering wheel and one stuck in the up position.
issues.next: Have the tilt motor, switch and wiring checked. Make sure the wheel is in a safe driving position before you drive.

issues.t: Musty or mildew smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A musty, moldy smell from the vents when the air conditioning is running, sometimes with a noisy blower.
issues.why: Moisture stays on the A/C evaporator and lets mold and debris build up. Mazda issued several bulletins on A/C odor and blower noise for these cars.
issues.next: Replace the cabin filter if fitted and have the evaporator cleaned with an approved treatment. Turning off the A/C a few minutes before you park helps it dry out.

issues.t: Water leaking under the passenger side of the dash
issues.sym: Wet carpet or water dripping on the front passenger floor, usually after using the air conditioning.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for the A/C cooling unit leaking water under the passenger-side dashboard instead of draining outside.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain and cooling unit checked and repaired. Dry the carpet promptly to avoid mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Blower motor noisy, wrong speed or not working
issues.sym: The heater or A/C fan runs at the wrong speed, makes noise, or stops blowing completely.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for blower motors with incorrect fan speed or no operation, and for blower noise caused by debris getting into the unit.
issues.next: Have the blower motor, its resistor and the housing checked for debris. Without airflow, the windshield can't be defrosted, so fix it before winter.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working
issues.sym: The wipers suddenly stop and may start again after a while.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for wiper motors that stop when an internal circuit breaker trips.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the wipers stop in rain. Have the wiper motor and linkage checked for binding or a failing motor.

issues.t: Low fuel light on but tank only takes 10-13 gallons
issues.sym: The low fuel warning comes on, but when you fill up the tank only takes about 10 to 13 gallons.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for this low fuel warning that comes on too early on some cars.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups to learn your real range, and ask a Mazda dealer about the bulletin fix for the fuel gauge sender.

issues.t: Highway speed surge on S models
issues.sym: On the highway at 55 to 70 mph, the car gently surges up and down by 1 to 3 mph without you changing the pedal.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for Millenia S models that surge slightly at steady highway speeds.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer or specialist about the bulletin fix. Also have vacuum lines and the throttle body checked, since leaks and dirt can make it worse.

issues.t: Squealing or rubbing noise from the drive belt
issues.sym: A squeal or rubbing sound from the front of the engine, often on startup or with the A/C on.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for drive belt noise on these cars. A worn belt, tensioner or pulley is usually the cause.
issues.next: Have the belt, tensioner and pulleys inspected and replace worn parts. A belt that breaks will stop the alternator and power steering.

issues.t: Airbag warning light on with codes 26 or 37
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light comes on and stays on.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for the airbag light coming on with codes 26 and/or 37 on these cars.
issues.next: Have the airbag system codes read and repaired. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on.

issues.t: Evaporative system code P1455 turns on check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P1455. The car drives normally.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for check engine lights caused by an evaporative emissions (fuel vapor) system fault, code P1455.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap is tight and the seal is not cracked. If the light returns, have the vapor system smoke-tested for leaks.

issues.t: Rattling noise from the exhaust system
issues.sym: A tinny rattle from under the car, often at idle or at certain engine speeds.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for rattling from the exhaust system. Loose heat shields and worn hangers are typical causes.
issues.next: Have the exhaust checked for loose shields, clamps and hangers. Also check for leaks, since exhaust fumes should not get into the cabin.
